input: Source reclaimed wood for a custom coffee table

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The species, condition, dimensions, and quantity of wood needed directly determine where to look and what to ask for — a rough slab is sourced very differently from finished planks.
Whether the user is in a rural, suburban, or urban area — and their country or region — determines which suppliers, salvage yards, or online marketplaces are actually accessible.
A strict budget ceiling changes whether reclaimed lumber yards, Facebook Marketplace finds, or premium curated suppliers are realistic options.
Knowing whether this is a solo DIY build, a commission for a client, or a collaboration with a carpenter affects how much guidance and quantity precision is needed.
The desired aesthetic — rustic and distressed vs. clean and refined — drives which wood types, grain patterns, and surface finishes are worth prioritising when sourcing.
Whether the user can transport large slabs themselves or needs delivery shapes which suppliers are practical, and whether the wood needs to be pre-milled or can arrive rough.

Understanding what 'successfully sourced' means — e.g., wood in hand by a specific date, a shortlist of vetted suppliers, or a confirmed purchase — defines what the end of this task actually looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Source reclaimed wood for a custom coffee table
gold.taskDescription: Find and acquire suitable reclaimed wood material to use in building a custom coffee table.

questions.title: What wood species, dimensions, and quantity do you need?
questions.description: Clarify the specific type of reclaimed wood (e.g., oak, pine, barn wood), the approximate size of pieces required, and how much total wood is needed for the table.

questions.title: What city or region are you sourcing from?
questions.description: Identify the user's location to determine which local salvage yards, lumber yards, or regional online marketplaces are realistically accessible.

questions.title: What is your total budget for the wood material?
questions.description: Establish a budget ceiling to filter sourcing options between free/cheap finds, mid-range salvage, and premium reclaimed lumber dealers.

questions.title: Is this a personal DIY build or a project for someone else?
questions.description: Determine whether this is a solo hobby project, a professional commission, or a collaborative build, as this affects precision requirements and urgency.

questions.title: What aesthetic are you going for — rustic or refined?
questions.description: Understand the desired look and feel of the finished table to prioritise the right wood character, distressing level, and surface texture when evaluating sources.

questions.title: Can you transport large pieces, or do you need delivery?
questions.description: Find out whether the user has means to pick up heavy or large slabs, or if they require suppliers who offer shipping or delivery, which narrows viable options significantly.

questions.title: What does success look like — a purchase, or a shortlist?
questions.description: Clarify whether the task ends with wood physically acquired, a confirmed order placed, or simply a vetted list of suppliers to choose from.
